practice1.hint: A bare except returns 0 for a missing file and also for a typo in your own code, a file full of words, and every mistake you have not made yet. Name the one error you are ready for.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with `except:` on its own?
choices: It catches every error, including bugs in your own code, and hides them
questions.explain: A bare except swallows the error you were expecting and the one you were not, so a real bug quietly turns into a wrong answer.

questions.prompt: When does the else block of a try run?
choices: Only when the try block raised nothing
Only when the try block raised something
questions.explain: else is the "nothing went wrong" branch. It keeps the code that depends on success out of the try, where it could raise and be caught by mistake.

questions.prompt: When does the finally block run?
choices: Every time, whichever of those happened
questions.explain: finally is for the cleanup that has to happen either way, which is the same job the with statement does for files.

questions.prompt: Put these lines in order so a missing file is reported instead of crashing.
questions.explain: The risky work goes inside try, and the except that names the error it might raise comes straight after the block, not before it.

questions.prompt: Which of these belong inside the try block when reading a file that might be missing?
choices: The import at the top of the program
The message printed when it all worked
questions.explain: Only the lines that can raise the error you are handling. Anything else in there is a line whose own failures you have quietly agreed to ignore.
